construction_markdown:
Let `p(T)=T^16+T^5+T^3+T+1`. It is irreducible over `F_2`: a Rabin certificate is `T^(2^16) ≡ T (mod p)` and `gcd(p,T^(2^8)-T)=1`. Put `E=F_2[T]/(p)` and `θ=T mod p`.

Let `A=span_{F_2}{1,θ,…,θ^14}⊂E`, so `|A|=2^15`. Order `A` by polynomial-basis coefficient vectors. Every `z∈E` is uniquely `z=z_0+z_1θ+⋯+z_15θ^15`. Define its binary inner block, indexed lexicographically by `y=(y_1,…,y_15)∈F_2^15`, by

`Φ(z)_y = z_0 + Σ_{i=1}^{15} z_i y_i`.

Thus `Φ:E→RM(1,15)` is an `F_2`-linear bijection.

For every polynomial `P(X)=Σ_{j=0}^{64} a_jX^j∈E[X]`, define

`c_P = ( Φ(P(α))_y )_{(α,y)∈A×F_2^15}`,

with lexicographic block and within-block ordering. Let `C={c_P:deg P≤64}`. Every field, basis, evaluation point, message coefficient, and coordinate order is fixed symbolically; there is no shortening, puncturing, padding, sampling, or random choice.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For integers `s≥1`, `L≤2^(s+1)`, and `0≤t<L`, evaluate degree-at-most-`t` polynomials over `F_{2^(s+1)}` at `L` fixed distinct points and concatenate each symbol through `RM(1,s)`. This deterministically gives a binary linear code with parameters `[L·2^s,(s+1)(t+1),≥(L−t)2^(s−1)]_2`.
discussion_posts.subject: RS–Hadamard concatenation lemma

discussion_posts.body_markdown: The candidate is optimal among concatenations certified solely by inner distance `2^14` and outer symbol distance `32704`. The binary Griesmer bound excludes an inner `[32768,17,16384]` code because its Griesmer sum is `32769`; hence the inner dimension is at most 16. Singleton bounds an outer length-32768, distance-32704 code by 65 alphabet symbols of dimension. Therefore the binary dimension is at most `16·65=1040`.
discussion_posts.subject: Sharp ceiling for the product-distance architecture

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Even one binary degree-65 direction cannot be added to the full degree-at-most-64 outer space. For each 65-set `S⊂A`, its coset contains `a∏_{s∈S}(X−s)`. Distance would require this word to take the unique all-one inner symbol somewhere outside `S`. Counting such incidences gives at most `N/65·C(N−1,64)=C(N,65)`, where `N=32768`. Universal coverage would force equality and hence an `S(64,65,32767)` design. Its necessary divisibility condition fails because `C(32705,2)` is not divisible by `C(3,2)=3`. Thus some 65-root word has only `N−65` balanced blocks and violates the target.

distance_audit: Because `C` is binary linear, pairwise distances reduce to weights of nonzero codewords.
A nonzero outer polynomial of degree at most 64 has at most 64 roots, hence at least 32704 nonzero blocks.
For `z≠0`, `Φ(z)` has weight `2^14`, except `Φ(1)`, which has weight `2^15`; therefore every nonzero block has weight at least `2^14`.
A deterministic scaled 64-root polynomial avoids the exceptional symbol 1 on every nonroot block, proving that the lower bound is attained exactly.
explicitness_audit: The sole outer field is the explicit quotient by `T^16+T^5+T^3+T+1`, with a Rabin irreducibility certificate.
The evaluation set is the explicitly specified 15-dimensional coefficient hyperplane in the polynomial basis.
The inner symbol map is the displayed coefficient-to-affine-function bijection.
Both coordinate orders use binary polynomial-basis vectors lexicographically.
The equality witness chooses the first 64 evaluation points and the lexicographically first admissible nonzero scale; at most 32704 of 65535 scales are forbidden.
There are no inherited parameters, floors, padding coordinates, punctures, or probabilistic choices.

proof_markdown:
### Theorem

The construction above is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters

`[1,073,741,824, 1,040, 535,822,336]_2`.

### Proof

The displayed Rabin congruence and gcd certify that `p` is irreducible, so `E` is the explicitly represented field with `2^16` elements. The vectors `1,θ,…,θ^15` form its polynomial basis; consequently `A` contains exactly `2^15` distinct elements.

The map `Φ` is `F_2`-linear. If `Φ(z)=0`, evaluation at `y=0` gives `z_0=0`, and the linear form `Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i` vanishes for every `y`; hence all `z_i=0`. Thus `Φ` is injective, and by equal dimensions it is a bijection onto `RM(1,15)`. If `(z_1,…,z_15)≠0`, its affine function is balanced and has weight `2^14`. The only other nonzero possibility is `z=1`, whose image is the all-one block of weight `2^15`.

The message space contains 65 freely chosen coefficients in `E`, so it has binary dimension `65·16=1040`. Its evaluation map is injective: a polynomial of degree at most 64 that vanished on all `|A|=32768` points would have more roots than its degree and hence would be zero. Composing this evaluation map with the injective block map `Φ` proves both binary linearity and dimension 1040. The coordinate set has size `|A|·2^15=2^30`.

Let `P` be nonzero. It has at most 64 roots in `A`, so at least `32768−64=32704` outer symbols are nonzero. Every corresponding inner block has weight at least `2^14`. Therefore

`wt(c_P) ≥ 32704·2^14 = (2^15−2^6)2^14 = 2^29−2^20 = 535,822,336`.

It remains to show equality. Let `R` be the first 64 elements of `A` and put `P_0(X)=∏_{r∈R}(X−r)`. For each `α∈A\R`, exactly one nonzero scalar `λ=P_0(α)^(−1)` would make `λP_0(α)=1`. Thus at most 32704 of the 65535 nonzero scalars are forbidden. Choose the lexicographically first un-forbidden `λ`. Then `P_*=λP_0` is zero exactly on the 64 points of `R`, while every other evaluated symbol is neither 0 nor 1. Its 64 root blocks have weight zero and all remaining 32704 blocks have weight exactly `2^14`. Hence

`wt(c_{P_*})=32704·2^14=535,822,336`.

The lower bound is therefore attained, proving the exact minimum distance.
